Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|12=draft}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa

{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|12=draft}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|12=draft}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|12=draft}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|12=draft}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|12=draft}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|12=draft}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|12=draft}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|12=draft}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺|12=draft}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡|12=draft}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|12=draft}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|12=draft}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀|12=draft}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川|12=draft}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川|12=draft}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|12=draft}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|12=draft}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|12=draft}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省|12=draft}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}

While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|12=draft}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|12=draft}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|12=draft}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|12=draft}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|12=draft}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|12=draft}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|12=draft}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|12=draft}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺|12=draft}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡|12=draft}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|12=draft}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|12=draft}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀|12=draft}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川|12=draft}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川|12=draft}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|12=draft}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|12=draft}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|12=draft}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省|12=draft}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}
{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|12=draft}}.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} with human face engraving
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved human face detail
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} == Interred Individual == {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}'s actual interred individual is unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} designates the tomb as the burial site of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}}, the third son of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft}}. {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} held prominent positions such as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of rebellion in 807. He and his mother, {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshiko|ja|藤原吉子|12=draft}}, were exiled to {{ill|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺|12=draft}}, where they took their own lives. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|12=draft}} (Kyoto City, Nakagyō-ku) - Exhibits {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}. * {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|12=draft}} (Kyoto City, Kamigyō-ku) - Exhibits artifacts from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|12=draft}} * {{ill|Uji Kofun Cluster|ja|宇治古墳群|12=draft}} {{draft categories| [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto]] [[Category:Fushimi Ward History]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fushimi-ku]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[Category:伝高畠陵古墳]] }} [[sn:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:%E9%BB%84%E9%87%91%E5%A1%9A2%E5%8F%B7%E5%A2%B3]] [[sn:yohata Tomb 2]] [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[ja:&action=edit]] {{citation needed|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} {{citation needed|Kyohata Tomb 2}} [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]][[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]][[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] {{Kofun navbar}}

Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|12=draft}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa

Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|12=draft}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa with engraved face
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved face detail
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|12=draft}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|12=draft}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|12=draft}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|12=draft}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|12=draft}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|12=draft}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|12=draft}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|12=draft}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺|12=draft}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡|12=draft}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|12=draft}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|12=draft}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀|12=draft}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川|12=draft}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川|12=draft}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|12=draft}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|12=draft}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|12=draft}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省|12=draft}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}
{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|12=draft}}.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} with human face engraving
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved human face detail
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} == Interred Individual == {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}'s actual interred individual is unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} designates the tomb as the burial site of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}}, the third son of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft}}. {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} held prominent positions such as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of rebellion in 807. He and his mother, {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshiko|ja|藤原吉子|12=draft}}, were exiled to {{ill|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺|12=draft}}, where they took their own lives. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|12=draft}} (Kyoto City, Nakagyō-ku) - Exhibits {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}. * {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|12=draft}} (Kyoto City, Kamigyō-ku) - Exhibits artifacts from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|12=draft}} * {{ill|Uji Kofun Cluster|ja|宇治古墳群|12=draft}} {{draft categories| }} {{citation needed|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} {{citation needed|Kyohata Tomb 2}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{draft categories| [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto]] [[Category:Fushimi Ward History]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fushimi-ku]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[Category:伝高畠陵古墳]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]][[Category:qq]] }} [[sn:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:%E9%BB%84%E9%87%91%E5%A1%9A2%E5%8F%B7%E5%A2%B3]] [[sn:yohata Tomb 2]] [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[ja:&action=edit]]

While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|12=draft}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|12=draft}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|12=draft}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|12=draft}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|12=draft}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|12=draft}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|12=draft}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|12=draft}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺|12=draft}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡|12=draft}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|12=draft}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|12=draft}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀|12=draft}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川|12=draft}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川|12=draft}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|12=draft}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|12=draft}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|12=draft}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省|12=draft}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}
{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|12=draft}}.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} with human face engraving
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved human face detail
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} == Interred Individual == {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}'s actual interred individual is unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} designates the tomb as the burial site of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}}, the third son of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft}}. {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} held prominent positions such as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of rebellion in 807. He and his mother, {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshiko|ja|藤原吉子|12=draft}}, were exiled to {{ill|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺|12=draft}}, where they took their own lives. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|12=draft}} (Kyoto City, Nakagyō-ku) - Exhibits {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}. * {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|12=draft}} (Kyoto City, Kamigyō-ku) - Exhibits artifacts from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|12=draft}} * {{ill|Uji Kofun Cluster|ja|宇治古墳群|12=draft}} {{draft categories| }} {{citation needed|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} {{citation needed|Kyohata Tomb 2}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{draft categories| [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto]] [[Category:Fushimi Ward History]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fushimi-ku]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[Category:伝高畠陵古墳]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]][[Category:qq]] }} [[sn:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:%E9%BB%84%E9%87%91%E5%A1%9A2%E5%8F%B7%E5%A2%B3]] [[sn:yohata Tomb 2]] [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[ja:&action=edit]]

So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:01, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Japanese Kofun |name = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |image = [[File:Tomb of Prince Iyo, entrance.jpg|280px]]
Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|12=draft}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa with engraved face
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved face detail
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|12=draft}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa with engraved face
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved face detail
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|12=draft}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|12=draft}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|12=draft}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|12=draft}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|12=draft}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|12=draft}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|12=draft}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|12=draft}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺|12=draft}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡|12=draft}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|12=draft}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|12=draft}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀|12=draft}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川|12=draft}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川|12=draft}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|12=draft}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|12=draft}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|12=draft}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省|12=draft}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}
{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|12=draft}}.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} with human face engraving
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved human face detail
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} == Interred Individual == {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}'s actual interred individual is unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} designates the tomb as the burial site of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}}, the third son of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft}}. {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} held prominent positions such as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of rebellion in 807. He and his mother, {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshiko|ja|藤原吉子|12=draft}}, were exiled to {{ill|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺|12=draft}}, where they took their own lives. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|12=draft}} (Kyoto City, Nakagyō-ku) - Exhibits {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}. * {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|12=draft}} (Kyoto City, Kamigyō-ku) - Exhibits artifacts from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|12=draft}} * {{ill|Uji Kofun Cluster|ja|宇治古墳群|12=draft}} {{draft categories| }} {{citation needed|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} {{citation needed|Kyohata Tomb 2}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{draft categories| [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto]] [[Category:Fushimi Ward History]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fushimi-ku]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[Category:伝高畠陵古墳]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]][[Category:qq]] }} [[sn:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:%E9%BB%84%E9%87%91%E5%A1%9A2%E5%8F%B7%E5%A2%B3]] [[sn:yohata Tomb 2]] [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[ja:&action=edit]]

While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|12=draft}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|12=draft}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|12=draft}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|12=draft}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|12=draft}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀|12=draft}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|12=draft}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa

Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|12=draft}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa

{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|12=draft}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|12=draft}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|12=draft}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|12=draft}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|12=draft}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|12=draft}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|12=draft}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|12=draft}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺|12=draft}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡|12=draft}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|12=draft}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|12=draft}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀|12=draft}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川|12=draft}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川|12=draft}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|12=draft}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|12=draft}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|12=draft}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|12=draft}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省|12=draft}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}

Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa
