He and his mother, {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshiko|ja|藤原吉子}}, were exiled to {{ill|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺}}, where they took their own lives. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館}} (Kyoto City, Nakagyō-ku) - Exhibits {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}. * {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館}} (Kyoto City, Kamigyō-ku) - Exhibits artifacts from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun}} * {{ill|Uji Kofun Cluster|ja|宇治古墳群}} {{draft categories| }} {{citation needed|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} {{citation needed|Kyohata Tomb 2}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{draft categories| [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto]] [[Category:Fushimi Ward History]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fushimi-ku]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[Category:伝高畠陵古墳]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]][[Category:qq]] }} [[sn:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:%E9%BB%84%E9%87%91%E5%A1%9A2%E5%8F%B7%E5%A2%B3]] [[sn:yohata Tomb 2]] [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[ja:&action=edit]]

Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa with engraved face
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved face detail
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}
{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館}}.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} with human face engraving
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved human face detail
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} == Interred Individual == {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}'s actual interred individual is unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates the tomb as the burial site of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō}}, the third son of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}}. {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō}} held prominent positions such as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of rebellion in 807. He and his mother, {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshiko|ja|藤原吉子}}, were exiled to {{ill|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺}}, where they took their own lives. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館}} (Kyoto City, Nakagyō-ku) - Exhibits {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}. * {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館}} (Kyoto City, Kamigyō-ku) - Exhibits artifacts from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun}} * {{ill|Uji Kofun Cluster|ja|宇治古墳群}} {{draft categories| }} {{citation needed|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} {{citation needed|Kyohata Tomb 2}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{draft categories| [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto]] [[Category:Fushimi Ward History]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fushimi-ku]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[Category:伝高畠陵古墳]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]][[Category:qq]] }} [[sn:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:%E9%BB%84%E9%87%91%E5%A1%9A2%E5%8F%B7%E5%A2%B3]] [[sn:yohata Tomb 2]] [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[ja:&action=edit]]

高さ9m（後円部） |埋葬施設 = [[粘土槨]] |出土品 = 冑小札・円形金具・[[埴輪]] |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[4世紀]]後半 |被葬者 = （[[宮内庁]]治定）[[伊予親王]] |陵墓 = [[宮内庁]]治定「巨幡墓」 |史跡 = なし |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = |地図 = Japan Kyoto city |アイコン = 前方後円墳-南西 |ラベル = 黄金塚2号墳 |ラベル位置 = top }} '''黄金塚2号墳'''（こがねづかにごうふん、遠山黄金塚2号墳）は、[[京都府]][[京都市]][[伏見区]]遠山にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[前方後円墳]]。 実際の被葬者は明らかでないが、後円部墳頂の五輪塔が[[宮内庁]]により「'''巨幡墓'''（こはたのはか）」として第50代[[桓武天皇]]第三[[皇子]]の[[伊予親王]]の墓に治定されている。 == 概要 == [[ファイル:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|盾形埴輪}}{{small|[[京都市考古資料館]]展示。}}]] [[京都盆地]]南東部、東山連峰最南端の大岩山南麓の丘陵上に築造された大型前方後円墳である{{Sfn|黄金塚古墳（平凡社）|1981}}。本古墳の北西にも大型前方後円墳として黄金塚1号墳（推定全長100メートル）が存在したが、現在までに失われている。[[1974年|1974]]・[[1981年|1981]]・[[1995年]]度（[[昭和]]49・56・[[平成]]7年度）に調査が実施されている。 墳形は前方後円形で、前方部を南西方向に向けるが、現在までに前方部は大きく破壊されている。墳丘長は約120メートルを測り、北山城地方および京都市内では最大規模になる{{Sfn|黄金塚2号墳（続古墳）|2002}}。墳丘外表では[[円筒埴輪]]列（盾形・朝顔形埴輪含む）が検出されている{{Sfn|黄金塚2号墳（続古墳）|2002}}。特に盾形埴輪は[[伝高畠陵古墳]]（[[向日市]]）付近の乾垣内遺跡出土埴輪棺と同工品とされる。埋葬施設は[[粘土槨]]で、昭和56年度調査で確認された際に、副葬品として革綴冑の小札・円形金具が検出されている{{Sfn|黄金塚2号墳（続古墳）|2002}}。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]]前期の[[4世紀]]後半頃と推定される{{Sfn|黄金塚2号墳（続古墳）|2002}}。被葬者は丘陵の西に広がる平野を生産基盤としたと想定され、[[巨椋池]]・[[淀川|宇治川]]・[[淀川]]をつなぐ水路および巨椋池・山科・近江をつなぐ道を掌握した有力首長墓として重要視される古墳になる{{Sfn|黄金塚古墳（平凡社）|1981}}。被葬者は明らかでないが、現在は後円部墳頂の五輪塔が[[宮内庁]]により[[伊予親王]]（第50代[[桓武天皇]]第三[[皇子]]、[[807年]]死去）の墓に治定されている。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[江戸時代]]、『山城志』・『陵墓一隅抄』に伊予親王墓の記載。 * [[1884年]]（[[明治]]17年）1月、宮内省（現・[[宮内庁]]）により後円部墳頂の五輪塔が伊予親王巨幡墓に治定{{Sfn|巨幡墓（国史）}}。 * [[1974年]]度（[[昭和]]49年度）、巨幡墓壁面工事に伴う立会調査。粘土槨の確認、副葬品の出土（[[宮内庁書陵部]]、[[1976年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|黄金塚2号墳（続古墳）|2002}}。 * [[1981年]]度（昭和56年度）、前方部北側の発掘調査。遺構確認なし（京都府埋蔵文化財調査研究センター、[[1982年]]に概報刊行）{{Sfn|黄金塚2号墳（続古墳）|2002}}。 * [[1995年]]度（[[平成]]7年度）、後円部北側の発掘調査。埴輪列の検出（[[花園大学]]考古学研究室、[[1997年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|黄金塚2号墳（続古墳）|2002}}。 == 墳丘 == 墳丘の規模は次の通り（古地図に基づく推定復元値）{{Sfn|黄金塚2号墳（続古墳）|2002}}。 * 墳丘長：120メートル * 後円部 ** 直径：60メートル ** 高さ：9メートル * 前方部 ** 幅：50メートル ** 高さ：7メートル ファイル:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|朝顔形埴輪
{{small|[[花園大学歴史博物館]]展示。}} ファイル:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|盾形埴輪
{{small|花園大学歴史博物館展示。}} ファイル:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|人面線刻付盾形埴輪
{{small|花園大学歴史博物館展示。}} ファイル:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|人面線刻
{{small|花園大学歴史博物館展示。}} == 被葬者 == 黄金塚2号墳の実際の被葬者は明らかでないが、[[宮内庁]]では後円部墳頂の五輪塔を'''[[伊予親王]]'''（いよしんのう）の墓に治定している。伊予親王は第50代[[桓武天皇]]の第三皇子で、式部卿・中務卿兼大宰帥などを歴任したが、[[大同 (日本)|大同]]2年（[[807年]]）に謀反の疑いで母の[[藤原吉子]]とともに[[川原寺]]に幽閉され、親王位が剥奪された翌日の11月12日に母と服毒自殺した人物である{{Sfn|伊予親王（国史）}}。『[[延喜式]]』[[諸陵式|諸陵寮]]では遠墓の「巨幡墓」として記載され、[[山城国]][[宇治郡]]の所在で、兆域は東1町・西1町5段・南2町・北3町で守丁1人を毎年あてるとする{{Sfn|巨幡墓（国史）}}。 その後、[[中世]]期には陵の所在に関する所伝は喪失{{Sfn|巨幡墓（国史）}}。[[近世]]期の『山城志』・『陵墓一隅抄』では現在の場所を示しており、[[明治維新]]後の[[1884年]]（[[明治]]17年）1月に巨幡墓に治定された{{Sfn|巨幡墓（国史）}}。ただし前述のように、黄金塚2号墳の築造年代は伊予親王から大きく遡る4世紀後半頃とされる。 == 関連施設 == * [[花園大学歴史博物館]]（京都市[[中京区]]西ノ京壺ノ内町） - 黄金塚2号墳の出土埴輪を展示。 * [[京都市考古資料館]]（京都市[[上京区]]元伊佐町） - 黄金塚2号墳の出土埴輪を展示。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=|chapter=|title=[[国史大辞典 (昭和時代)|国史大辞典]]|publisher=[[吉川弘文館]]|isbn=|ref=}} ** {{Wikicite|reference=[[佐伯有清]]「伊予親王」|ref={{Harvid|伊予親王（国史）}}}}、{{Wikicite|reference=戸原純一「巨幡墓」（伊予親王項目内）|ref={{Harvid|巨幡墓（国史）}}}}。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1981|chapter=黄金塚古墳|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 27 京都市の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=4582910122|ref={{Harvid|黄金塚古墳（平凡社）|1981}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=丸川義広|year=2002|chapter=黄金塚2号墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典|続 日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490105991|ref={{Harvid|黄金塚2号墳（続古墳）|2002}}}} == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1976|chapter=巨幡墓の境界線崩壊防止工事の立会調査|title=書陵部紀要 第27号|publisher=[[宮内庁書陵部]]|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1982|chapter=黄金塚2号墳発掘調査概要|title={{PDFlink|[http://www.kyotofu-maibun.or.jp/data/kankou/kankou-pdf/gaihou/1-50/G004web.pdf 京都府遺跡調査概報 第4冊]}}|publisher=京都府埋蔵文化財調査研究センター|isbn=|pages=62-66|ref=}} - リンクは京都府埋蔵文化財調査研究センター。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1982|chapter=黄金塚2号墳|title={{PDFlink|[http://www.kyotofu-maibun.or.jp/data/kankou/kankou-pdf/jyouhou/kyoutofu-J003.pdf 京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第3号]}}|publisher=京都府埋蔵文化財調査研究センター|isbn=|page=54||ref=}} - リンクは京都府埋蔵文化財調査研究センター。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=黄金塚2号墳発掘調査団|author=|year=1997|chapter=|title=黄金塚2号墳の研究（花大考研報告10）|publisher=花園大学文学部考古学研究室|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == {{commonscat|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} * [[伊予親王]] * [[伝高畠陵古墳]] * [[宇治古墳群]] {{DEFAULTSORT:こかねつかにこうふん}} [[Category:京都府の古墳]] [[Category:伏見区の歴史]] [[Category:前方後円墳]] [[Category:日本の陵墓]]

{{small|花園大学歴史博物館展示。}} == 被葬者 == 黄金塚2号墳の実際の被葬者は明らかでないが、[[宮内庁]]では後円部墳頂の五輪塔を'''[[伊予親王]]'''（いよしんのう）の墓に治定している。伊予親王は第50代[[桓武天皇]]の第三皇子で、式部卿・中務卿兼大宰帥などを歴任したが、[[大同 (日本)|大同]]2年（[[807年]]）に謀反の疑いで母の[[藤原吉子]]とともに[[川原寺]]に幽閉され、親王位が剥奪された翌日の11月12日に母と服毒自殺した人物である{{Sfn|伊予親王（国史）}}。『[[延喜式]]』[[諸陵式|諸陵寮]]では遠墓の「巨幡墓」として記載され、[[山城国]][[宇治郡]]の所在で、兆域は東1町・西1町5段・南2町・北3町で守丁1人を毎年あてるとする{{Sfn|巨幡墓（国史）}}。 その後、[[中世]]期には陵の所在に関する所伝は喪失{{Sfn|巨幡墓（国史）}}。[[近世]]期の『山城志』・『陵墓一隅抄』では現在の場所を示しており、[[明治維新]]後の[[1884年]]（[[明治]]17年）1月に巨幡墓に治定された{{Sfn|巨幡墓（国史）}}。ただし前述のように、黄金塚2号墳の築造年代は伊予親王から大きく遡る4世紀後半頃とされる。 == 関連施設 == * [[花園大学歴史博物館]]（京都市[[中京区]]西ノ京壺ノ内町） - Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa

{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}

{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} == Interred Individual == {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}'s actual interred individual is unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates the tomb as the burial site of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō}}, the third son of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}}. {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō}} held prominent positions such as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of rebellion in 807. He and his mother, {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshiko|ja|藤原吉子}}, were exiled to {{ill|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺}}, where they took their own lives. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館}} (Kyoto City, Nakagyō-ku) - Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa

{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|12=draft}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|12=draft}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|12=draft}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|12=draft}}, Kyoto Prefecture. Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa

{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=draft}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|qq=draft}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|qq=draft}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|qq=draft}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|qq=draft}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|qq=draft}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺|qq=draft}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡|qq=draft}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|qq=draft}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀|qq=draft}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池|qq=draft}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川|qq=draft}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川|qq=draft}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|qq=draft}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|qq=draft}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省|qq=draft}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft}}

{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=draft}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|qq=draft}}, Kyoto Prefecture. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|qq=draft}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|qq=draft}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|qq=draft}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省|qq=draft}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft}}

However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}} designates the tomb as the burial site of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft}}, the third son of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft}}. {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft}} held prominent positions such as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of rebellion in 807. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft}} in [[Muko City]]. He and his mother, {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshiko|ja|藤原吉子|qq=draft}}, were exiled to {{ill|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺|qq=draft}}, where they took their own lives. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|qq=draft}} (Kyoto City, Nakagyō-ku) - Exhibits {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft}}. * {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|qq=draft}} (Kyoto City, Kamigyō-ku) - Exhibits artifacts from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Uji Kofun Cluster|ja|宇治古墳群|qq=draft}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|黄金塚2号墳|version=99995551|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto]] [[Category:Fushimi Ward History]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fushimi-ku]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] }} [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[sn:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:%E9%BB%84%E9%87%91%E5%A1%9A2%E5%8F%B7%E5%A2%B3]] [[sn:yohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:&action=edit]]

Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa with engraved face
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved face detail
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8=ja|qq=}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|qq=}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Kanmu|qq=}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|qq=}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōiwadake Mountain|qq=}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashiyama Range|qq=}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|qq=}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa coffin|qq=}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inukakiuchi site|qq=}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatake Tomb|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/clay-coffer type|13=User:Immanuelle/Clay coffin chamber|qq=}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/4th century|qq=}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Ogura|qq=}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji River|qq=}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yodo River|qq=}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro-shi|qq=}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|qq=}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of the Imperial Household|qq=}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}
{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanazono University Museum of History|qq=}}.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}} with human face engraving
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved human face detail
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} == Interred Individual == {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}'s actual interred individual is unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} designates the tomb as the burial site of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}}, the third son of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Kanmu|qq=}}. {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} held prominent positions such as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of rebellion in 807. He and his mother, {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshiko|ja|藤原吉子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Yoshiko|qq=}}, were exiled to {{ill|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawara-dera|qq=}}, where they took their own lives. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanazono University Museum of History|qq=}} (Kyoto City, Nakagyō-ku) - Exhibits {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}} from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}. * {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|qq=}} (Kyoto City, Kamigyō-ku) - Exhibits artifacts from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatake Tomb|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Uji Kofun Cluster|ja|宇治古墳群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|黄金塚2号墳|version=99995551|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto]] [[Category:Fushimi Ward History]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fushimi-ku]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] }} [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[sn:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:%E9%BB%84%E9%87%91%E5%A1%9A2%E5%8F%B7%E5%A2%B3]] [[sn:yohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:&action=edit]]

Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa with engraved face
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved face detail
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8=ja|qq=}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|qq=}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Kanmu|qq=}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|qq=}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōiwadake Mountain|qq=}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashiyama Range|qq=}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|qq=}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa coffin|qq=}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inukakiuchi site|qq=}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatake Tomb|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/clay-coffer type|13=User:Immanuelle/Clay coffin chamber|qq=}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/4th century|qq=}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Ogura|qq=}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji River|qq=}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yodo River|qq=}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro-shi|qq=}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|qq=}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of the Imperial Household|qq=}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}

However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} designates the tomb as the burial site of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}}, the third son of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Kanmu|qq=}}. {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} held prominent positions such as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of rebellion in 807. He and his mother, {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshiko|ja|藤原吉子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Yoshiko|qq=}}, were exiled to {{ill|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawara-dera|qq=}}, where they took their own lives. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanazono University Museum of History|qq=}} (Kyoto City, Nakagyō-ku) - Exhibits {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}} from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}. * {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|qq=}} (Kyoto City, Kamigyō-ku) - Exhibits artifacts from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatake Tomb|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Uji Kofun Cluster|ja|宇治古墳群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|黄金塚2号墳|version=99995551|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto]] [[Category:Fushimi Ward History]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fushimi-ku]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] }} [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[sn:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:%E9%BB%84%E9%87%91%E5%A1%9A2%E5%8F%B7%E5%A2%B3]] [[sn:yohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:&action=edit]]
