{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8=ja|qq=}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|qq=}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Kanmu|qq=}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|qq=}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōiwadake Mountain|qq=}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashiyama Range|qq=}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|qq=}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa coffin|qq=}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inukakiuchi site|qq=}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatake Tomb|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/clay-coffer type|13=User:Immanuelle/Clay coffin chamber|qq=}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/4th century|qq=}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Ogura|qq=}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji River|qq=}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yodo River|qq=}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro-shi|qq=}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|qq=}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of the Imperial Household|qq=}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}

However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} designates the tomb as the burial site of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}}, the third son of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Kanmu|qq=}}. {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} held prominent positions such as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of rebellion in 807. He and his mother, {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshiko|ja|藤原吉子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Yoshiko|qq=}}, were exiled to {{ill|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawara-dera|qq=}}, where they took their own lives. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanazono University Museum of History|qq=}} (Kyoto City, Nakagyō-ku) - Exhibits {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}} from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}. * {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|qq=}} (Kyoto City, Kamigyō-ku) - Exhibits artifacts from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatake Tomb|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Uji Kofun Cluster|ja|宇治古墳群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|黄金塚2号墳|version=99995551|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto]] [[Category:Fushimi Ward History]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fushimi-ku]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] }} [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[sn:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:%E9%BB%84%E9%87%91%E5%A1%9A2%E5%8F%B7%E5%A2%B3]] [[sn:yohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:&action=edit]]

Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa

Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8=ja|qq=}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|qq=}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Kanmu|qq=}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|qq=}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōiwadake Mountain|qq=}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashiyama Range|qq=}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|qq=}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa coffin|qq=}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inukakiuchi site|qq=}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatake Tomb|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/clay-coffer type|13=User:Immanuelle/Clay coffin chamber|qq=}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/4th century|qq=}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Ogura|qq=}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji River|qq=}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yodo River|qq=}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro-shi|qq=}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|qq=}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of the Imperial Household|qq=}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}
{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanazono University Museum of History|qq=}}.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}} with human face engraving
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved human face detail
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} == Interred Individual == {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}'s actual interred individual is unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} designates the tomb as the burial site of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}}, the third son of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Kanmu|qq=}}. {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} held prominent positions such as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of rebellion in 807. He and his mother, {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshiko|ja|藤原吉子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Yoshiko|qq=}}, were exiled to {{ill|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawara-dera|qq=}}, where they took their own lives. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanazono University Museum of History|qq=}} (Kyoto City, Nakagyō-ku) - Exhibits {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}} from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}. * {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|qq=}} (Kyoto City, Kamigyō-ku) - Exhibits artifacts from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatake Tomb|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Uji Kofun Cluster|ja|宇治古墳群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|黄金塚2号墳|version=99995551|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto]] [[Category:Fushimi Ward History]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fushimi-ku]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] }} [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[sn:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:%E9%BB%84%E9%87%91%E5%A1%9A2%E5%8F%B7%E5%A2%B3]] [[sn:yohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:&action=edit]]

Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa with engraved face
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved face detail
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8=ja|qq=}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|qq=}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|lt=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|lt=Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Kanmu|qq=}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|qq=}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōiwadake Mountain|qq=}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashiyama Range|qq=}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|qq=}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa coffin|qq=}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inukakiuchi site|qq=}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatake Tomb|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/clay-coffer type|13=User:Immanuelle/Clay coffin chamber|qq=}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/4th century|qq=}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Ogura|qq=}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji River|qq=}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yodo River|qq=}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro-shi|qq=}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|qq=}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|lt=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|lt=Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of the Imperial Household|qq=}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}
{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanazono University Museum of History|qq=}}.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}} with human face engraving
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved human face detail
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} == Interred Individual == {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}'s actual interred individual is unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} designates the tomb as the burial site of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}}, the third son of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Kanmu|qq=}}. {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} held prominent positions such as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of rebellion in 807. He and his mother, {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshiko|ja|藤原吉子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Yoshiko|qq=}}, were exiled to {{ill|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawara-dera|qq=}}, where they took their own lives. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanazono University Museum of History|qq=}} (Kyoto City, Nakagyō-ku) - Exhibits {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}} from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}. * {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|qq=}} (Kyoto City, Kamigyō-ku) - Exhibits artifacts from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatake Tomb|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Uji Kofun Cluster|ja|宇治古墳群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|黄金塚2号墳|version=99995551|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto]] [[Category:Fushimi Ward History]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fushimi-ku]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] }} [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[sn:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:%E9%BB%84%E9%87%91%E5%A1%9A2%E5%8F%B7%E5%A2%B3]] [[sn:yohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:&action=edit]]

Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa with engraved face
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved face detail
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8=ja|qq=}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|qq=}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|lt=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|lt=Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Kanmu|qq=}}). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|qq=}}.}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}} is a large {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōiwadake Mountain|qq=}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashiyama Range|qq=}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|qq=}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa coffin|qq=}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inukakiuchi site|qq=}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatake Tomb|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/clay-coffer type|13=User:Immanuelle/Clay coffin chamber|qq=}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/4th century|qq=}} during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}}. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Ogura|qq=}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji River|qq=}}, and the {{ill|Yodo River|ja|淀川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yodo River|qq=}}. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}}. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro-shi|qq=}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|qq=}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|lt=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|lt=Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}} by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|ja|宮内省|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of the Imperial Household|qq=}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}}). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}
{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanazono University Museum of History|qq=}}.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}
{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}} with human face engraving

{{small|Hanazono University Museum of History.}} == Interred Individual == {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}'s actual interred individual is unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} designates the tomb as the burial site of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}}, the third son of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Kanmu|qq=}}. {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} held prominent positions such as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of rebellion in 807. He and his mother, {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshiko|ja|藤原吉子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Yoshiko|qq=}}, were exiled to {{ill|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawara-dera|qq=}}, where they took their own lives. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Hanazono University Museum of History|ja|花園大学歴史博物館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanazono University Museum of History|qq=}} (Kyoto City, Nakagyō-ku) - Exhibits {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}} from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}. * {{ill|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|ja|京都市考古資料館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|qq=}} (Kyoto City, Kamigyō-ku) - Exhibits artifacts from {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatake Tomb|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Uji Kofun Cluster|ja|宇治古墳群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|黄金塚2号墳|version=99995551|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto]] [[Category:Fushimi Ward History]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fushimi-ku]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] }} [[sn:Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun]] [[sn:Kyohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:%E9%BB%84%E9%87%91%E5%A1%9A2%E5%8F%B7%E5%A2%B3]] [[sn:yohata Tomb 2]] [[ja:&action=edit]]

Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa with engraved face
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved face detail
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8=ja|qq=}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|qq=}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|lt=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|lt=Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (the third prince of [[:en:Emperor Kanmu|Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]]}}{{small|Exhibited at [[:en:Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]].}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}} is a large [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōiwadake Mountain|qq=}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashiyama Range|qq=}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|qq=}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed. Excavations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section pointing southwest. However, much of the front section has been destroyed. The overall length of the mound measures approximately 120 meters, making it the largest tumulus in the Kita Yamashiro region and Kyoto City. Cylindrical [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], including shield-shaped and morning glory-shaped varieties, were discovered on the mound surface. Notably, shield-shaped haniwa are related to {{ill|haniwa coffin|ja|埴輪棺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa coffin|qq=}} found at the {{ill|Inukakiuchi site|ja|乾垣内遺跡|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inukakiuchi site|qq=}} near the {{ill|Den-Takabatake Tomb|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|1=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatake Tomb|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay-coffer type|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/clay-coffer type|13=User:Immanuelle/Clay coffin chamber|qq=}}, confirmed during the 1974 survey, with artifacts such as leather armor plates and circular fittings unearthed. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late [[:en:4th century|4th century]] during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]]. The individual buried here likely controlled the fertile plains to the west of the mound, which served as an important production base, and had influence over waterways connecting {{ill|Lake Ogura|ja|巨椋池|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Ogura|qq=}}, the {{ill|Uji River|ja|宇治川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji River|qq=}}, and the [[:en:Yodo River|Yodo River]]. The tomb is considered a key site for studying regional politics. The tumulus is now identified as the Kohata Tomb, believed to be the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (d. 807), based on the designation by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]. == History == * '''Edo period''': Mention of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}}'s tomb in historical texts such as *{{ill|Yamashiro-shi|ja|山城志|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro-shi|qq=}}* and *{{ill|Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|ja|陵墓一隅抄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōbo Ichigu-shō|qq=}}*. * '''1884 (Meiji 17)''': Designated as the {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|lt=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|lt=Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}} by the [[:en:Ministry of the Imperial Household|Ministry of the Imperial Household]] (now the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]). * '''1974''': Wall construction work led to archaeological oversight, uncovering the clay coffer and grave goods. * '''1981''': Excavation on the northern side of the anterior part; no significant remains were identified. * '''1995''': Excavation on the northern side of the posterior part revealed haniwa rows. == Mound Dimensions == Estimated dimensions based on historical records and surveys: * Total mound length: 120 meters * Posterior portion: ''' Diameter: 60 meters ''' Height: 9 meters * Anterior portion: ''' Width: 50 meters ''' Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning glory-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]]

Rear circular mound (Iyo Prince's Kohata Tomb) |alternate_name = Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |Region = Kyoto Prefecture |location = [[Kyoto City]], [[Fushimi Ward]], Toyama |coordinates = {{coord|34|56|8.80|N|135|47|22.85|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}} |type = [[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped tumulus]] |area = Mound length: 120m
Height: 9m (rear mound) |burial = [[Clay chamber]] |burial goods = Armor map_sizes, circular fittings, [[haniwa]] |Associated tumuli = |built = Late [[4th century]] |Buried figure = (Imperial Household Agency) [[Prince Iyo]] |Imperial tomb = Designated by Imperial Household Agency as Kohata Tomb |Cultural property = None |omitted = JP-26 |map = Japan Kyoto city |type = Keyhole-shaped Kofun (southwest) |map_dot_label = Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun |map_dot_label = top }} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{lang|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun}}, {{lang|ja-Latn|Koganezuka Nigōfun}}), also referred to as '''Toyama Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''', is a large [[zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) located in Toyama, [[Fushimi-ku]], [[Kyoto]], Japan. While the actual individual buried in the mound remains unknown, the rear circular mound features a gorintō (five-ringed pagoda), which the [[Imperial Household Agency]] has officially Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (third prince of [[Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shield-shaped haniwa (Kyoto City Archaeological Museum exhibit)]] Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun is located at the southern foothills of Ōiwasan on the southeastern edge of the Kyoto Basin. The tumulus was part of a larger cluster of mounds, including the now-destroyed Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun, a keyhole-shaped tumulus with an estimated length of 100 meters. Archaeological investigations were conducted in 1974, 1981, and 1995. The mound faces southwest, though the frontal portion has suffered significant destruction. With an overall length of approximately 120 meters, it is the largest keyhole-shaped mound in the Kita-Yamashiro region and within Kyoto City. Excavations revealed a row of cylindrical haniwa, including shield- and morning-glory-shaped haniwa, suggesting connections with nearby tumuli such as the Dendengaito site near {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} in [[Muko City]]. The burial chamber, constructed as a clay enclosure, yielded burial goods such as lacquered armor map_sizes and circular metal fittings during a 1981 investigation. The tumulus is believed to date back to the late [[Kofun period]] (4th century). It likely served as the tomb for a prominent local leader who controlled access to the [[Ogura Pond]], [[Uji River]], and [[Yodo River]] water systems, as well as trade routes linking Ogura Pond, Yamashina, and [[Ōmi Province]]. == Excavation History == * [[Edo period]]: References to the tomb appear in documents such as the ''Yamashiro-shi'' and ''Ryōbo Ichigunshō''. * [[1884]] (Meiji 17): The rear mound was Historic Site1 as the Kohata Tomb, the resting place of Prince Iyo, by the [[Imperial Household Agency]]. * 1974 (Shōwa 49): Monitoring during wall repairs uncovered the clay burial chamber and burial goods (Imperial Household Agency). * 1981 (Shōwa 56): Excavations near the frontal section identified no significant remains (Kyoto Archaeological Research Center). * 1995 (Heisei 7): Investigations of the rear mound uncovered rows of haniwa (Hanazono University Archaeology Lab). == Kofun area == Estimated area based on ancient maps are as follows: * Total length: 120 meters * Rear mound: ** Diameter: 60 meters ** Height: 9 meters * Front mound: ** Width: 50 meters ** Height: 7 meters File:黄金塚2号墳出土 朝顔形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Morning-glory-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 (花大博展示).JPG|Shield-shaped haniwa with engraved face
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} File:黄金塚2号墳出土 人面線刻付盾形埴輪 人面線刻 (花大博展示).JPG|Engraved face detail
{{small|Hanazono University History Museum exhibit}} == Prince Iyo == The true occupant of the Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun remains uncertain. However, the rear circular mound's gorintō has been Historic Site1 as the tomb of Prince Iyo, the third son of Emperor Kanmu. Prince Iyo served as Minister of Ceremonial Affairs and Governor of Dazaifu but was accused of plotting treason in 807 CE. He and his mother, [[Fujiwara no Yoshiko]], were confined at Kawara-dera, where they committed suicide by poisoning. The ''[[Engishiki]]'' lists his tomb as "Kohata Tomb," located in Uji District, Yamashiro Province. While historical records confirm the Historic Site, the tumulus's 4th-century construction predates Prince Iyo's life by several centuries. == Related Facilities == * [[Hanazono University History Museum]] (Nishinokyo, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto): Exhibits haniwa from Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun. * [[Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]] (Motoyoshicho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto): Displays haniwa burial goods from the tumulus. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''Research on Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun'' (Hanazono Archaeological Report No. 10), Hanazono University, 1997. * ''Summary of Archaeological Findings in Kyoto Prefecture'' (Vol. 4), Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Center, 1982. == See Also == * {{ill|Iyo Shinnō|ja|伊予親王|lt=Prince Iyo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} * {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|8=ja|9=宇治古墳群|Uji Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8=ja|qq=}} '''Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun''' ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}}, Tōyama Koganezuka 2-gōfun) is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] located in {{ill|Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市伏見区遠山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōyama, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|qq=}}, Kyoto Prefecture. While the actual interred individual is not definitively known, the five-tiered pagoda atop the circular mound has been designated by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] as the "Kohata Tomb" ({{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|lt=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|lt=Kohata Tomb|ja|巨幡墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kohata Tomb|qq=}}), the burial place of {{ill|Prince Iyo|ja|伊予親王|1=Iyo Shinnō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Iyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shinnō|qq=}} (the third prince of [[:en:Emperor Kanmu|Emperor Kanmu]]). == Overview == [[File:黄金塚2号墳出土 盾形埴輪.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shield-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]]}}{{small|Exhibited at [[:en:Kyoto City Archaeological Museum|Kyoto City Archaeological Museum]].}}]] {{ill|Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|ja|黄金塚2号墳|1=Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 2 Kofun|qq=}} is a large [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] constructed in the southeastern Kyoto Basin, located on the southern slope of the {{ill|Ōiwadake Mountain|ja|大岩山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōiwadake Mountain|qq=}}, the southernmost peak of the {{ill|Higashiyama Range|ja|東山連峰|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashiyama Range|qq=}}. Another large keyhole-shaped tumulus, {{ill|Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|ja|黄金塚1号墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koganezuka No. 1 Kofun|qq=}}, once stood to the northwest but has been destroyed.
